sets.title: Mitsubishi MUZ-FS06–18NA/NAH outdoor (MSZ-FS wall-mount systems)
sets.note: Verified 2026-10-26. Source: Service manual OBH873B, 10-3 Troubleshooting Check Table (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED; blink count after each 2.5-second OFF). Uncertain: in the printed table, rows No.2 and No.3 have no separate LED-indication cell (they appear to share No.1's '1-time blink every 2.5 seconds'). Rows 17's remedy cell is blank as extracted. The indoor-unit failure-mode-recall table (10-2, PDF p.28) is not transcribed here.

rows.pattern: No.1: 1-time blink every 2.5 seconds (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Outdoor power system — Overcurrent protection cut-out operates 3 consecutive times within 1 minute after the compressor gets started.
rows.remedy: • Reconnect connector of compressor. • Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor". • Check stop valve.

rows.meaning: Outdoor thermistors — Discharge temperature thermistor, fin temperature thermistor, defrost thermistor, outdoor heat exchanger temperature thermistor or ambient temperature thermistor shorts or opens during compressor running. / P.C. board temperature thermistor shorts or opens during compressor running.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "Check of outdoor thermistors". • Replace inverter P.C. board.

rows.meaning: Outdoor control system — Nonvolatile memory data cannot be read properly. (The left lamp of the OPERATION INDICATOR lamp on the indoor unit lights up or blinks 7-time.)
rows.remedy: • Replace inverter P.C. board.

rows.pattern: No.4: 6-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Serial signal — The communication fails between the indoor and outdoor unit for 3 minutes.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "How to check miswiring and serial signal error.

rows.pattern: No.5: 11-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Stop valve/ Closed valve — Closed valve is detected by compressor current.
rows.remedy: • Check stop valve.

rows.pattern: No.6: 16-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: 4-way valve/ Pipe temperature — The 4-way valve does not work properly. The indoor coil thermistor detects an abnormal temperature.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "Check of R.V. coil". • Replace the inverter P.C. board.

rows.pattern: No.7: 17-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Outdoor refrigerant system abnormality — A closed valve and air trapped in the refrigerant circuit are detected based on the temperature sensed by the indoor and outdoor thermistors and the current of the compressor.
rows.remedy: • Check for a gas leak in a connecting piping etc. • Check the stop valve. • Refer to 10-5. “Check of outdoor refrigerant circuit”.

rows.pattern: No.8: 2-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Overcurrent protection — Large current flows into the power module (IC700).
rows.remedy: • Reconnect connector of compressor. • Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor". • Check stop valve.

rows.pattern: No.9: 3-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Discharge temperature overheat protection — Temperature of discharge temperature thermistor exceeds 241°F (116°C), compressor stops. Compressor can restart if discharge temperature thermistor reads 212°F (100°C) or less 3 minutes later.
rows.remedy: • Check refrigerant circuit and refrigerant amount. • Refer to 10-5. "Check of LEV".

rows.pattern: No.10: 4-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Fin temperature /P.C. board temperature thermistor overheat protection — Temperature of the fin temperature thermistor on the heat sink exceeds 167 - 187°F (75 - 86°C) (FS06/09/12)/167 - 176°F (75 - 80°C) (FS15/18) or temperature of P.C. board temperature thermistor on the inverter P.C.board exceeds 162 - 185°F (72 - 85°C) (FS06/09/12)/158 - 167°F (70 - 75°C) (FS15/18).
rows.remedy: • Check around outdoor unit. • Check outdoor unit air passage. • Refer to 10-5. "Check of outdoor fan motor".

rows.pattern: No.11: 5-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: High pressure protection — Indoor coil thermistor exceeds 158°F (70°C) in HEAT mode. Defrost thermistor exceeds 158°F (70°C) in COOL mode.
rows.remedy: • Check refrigerant circuit and refrigerant amount. • Check stop valve.

rows.pattern: No.12: 8-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Compressor synchronous abnormality — The waveform of compressor current is distorted.
rows.remedy: • Reconnect connector of compressor. • Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor".

rows.pattern: No.13: 10-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Outdoor fan motor — Outdoor fan has stopped 3 times in a row within 30 seconds after outdoor fan start-up.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "Check of outdoor fan motor. • Refer to 10-5. "Check of inverter P.C. board.

rows.pattern: No.14: 12-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Each phase current of compressor — Each phase current of compressor cannot be detected normally.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor".

rows.pattern: No.15: 13-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Bus-bar voltage (DC) — Bus-bar voltage of inverter cannot be detected normally.
rows.remedy: • It occurs with following case. Instantaneous power voltage drop. (Short time power failure) (FS15/18) • Refer to 10-5. "Check of power supply". (FS15/18) • Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor".

rows.pattern: No.16: 1-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Frequency drop by current protection — FS06/09/12 When the input current exceeds approximately 10A (FS06/09)/10.5A (FS12), compressor frequency lowers. / FS15/18 Current from power outlet is nearing breaker capacity.
rows.remedy: The unit is normal, but check the following. • Check if indoor filters are clogged. • Check if refrigerant is short. • Check if indoor/outdoor unit air circulation is short cycled.

rows.pattern: No.17: 3-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Frequency drop by high pressure protection — Temperature of indoor coil thermistor exceeds 131 °F (55°C) in HEAT mode, compressor frequency lowers. / Frequency drop by defrosting in COOL mode Indoor coil thermistor reads 46°F (8°C) or less in COOL mode, compressor frequency lowers.

rows.pattern: No.18: 4-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Frequency drop by discharge temperature protection — Temperature of discharge temperature thermistor exceeds 232°F (111°C), compressor frequency lowers.
rows.remedy: • Check refrigerant circuit and refrigerant amount. • Refer to 10-5. "Check of LEV". • Refer to 10-5. "Check of outdoor thermistors".

rows.pattern: No.19: MUZ-FS06/09/12 5-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Outside temperature thermistor protection — When the outside temperature thermistor shorts or opens, protective operation without that thermistor is performed.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. Check of outdoor thermistors.

rows.pattern: No.20: 7-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Low discharge temperature protection — Temperature of discharge temperature thermistor has been 122°F (50°C) or less for 20 minutes.
rows.remedy: • Refer to 10-5. "Check of LEV". • Check refrigerant circuit and refrigerant amount.

rows.pattern: No.21: 8-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: MUZ-FS06/09/12 PAM protection PAM: Pulse Amplitude Modulation — The overcurrent flows into PFC (Power factor correction :IC820) or the bus-bar voltage reaches 394 V or more, PAM stops and restarts. / MUZ-FS15/18 Zero cross detecting circuit Zero cross signal cannot be detected.
rows.remedy: This is not malfunction. PAM protection will be activated in the following cases: 1 Instantaneous power voltage drop. (Short time power failure) 2 When the power supply voltage is high. • It occurs with following cases. 1 Instantaneous power voltage drop. (Short time power failure) 2 Distortion of primary voltage • Refer to 10-5. "Check of power supply".

rows.pattern: No.22: 9-time blink 2.5 seconds OFF (outdoor inverter P.C. board LED)
rows.meaning: Inverter check mode — The connector of compressor is disconnected, inverter check mode starts.
rows.remedy: • Check if the connector of the compressor is correctly connected. Refer to 10-5. "How to check inverter/compressor".

sets.title: Rheem RA17
sets.note: Verified 2026-10-26. Source: Installation instructions 92-104921-07-06, ICC Diagnostic Codes (dual 7-segment LED). Remedy = the 'Status/Possible Cause – Troubleshooting Information' column.

rows.meaning: 0 – Standby: No command for unit operation
rows.remedy: Normal operation

rows.meaning: c - First Stage Cooling: Unit has received a command for first stage cooling
rows.remedy: Normal operation

rows.meaning: c - Anti-short cycle timer (3 minutes) or Minimum run timer (30 seconds) active
rows.remedy: • The unit has received a command for first stage cooling during an active anti-short cycle timer or minimum run timer. • Wait until unit timer has expired or press the TEST button to defeat short cycle delay.

rows.meaning: C - Second Stage Cooling: Unit has received a command for second stage cooling
rows.remedy: Normal operation

rows.meaning: C - Anti-short cycle timer (3 minutes) or Minimum run timer (30 seconds) active
rows.remedy: • The unit has received a command for second stage cooling during an active anti-short cycle timer or minimum run timer. • Wait unit timer has expired or press the TEST button to defeat short cycle delay.

rows.meaning: P – Protector Trip: A command for compressor operation is present but no current is measured to the compressor
rows.remedy: • Motor protector open • Line volta e disconnected [sic]

rows.meaning: 01 – Long Run Time (Compressor): The compressor has continuously run for more than 18 hours in the cooling mode.
rows.remedy: • Low refrigerant charge • Air ducts have substantial leakage • Dirty indoor air filter • Dirty outdoor coil

rows.meaning: 02 – High Side Fault: Compressor limit has opened four (4) times within a call for operation
rows.remedy: • Outdoor coil is dirty (cooling mode) • Outdoor fan is not running (cooling mode) • Dirty indoor coil or filter (heating mode) • Indoor blower is not running (heating mode) • Liquid line restriction • Excessive refrigerant charge

rows.meaning: 03 – Short Cycling: The ICC detects the run time for the past four (4) compressor cycles is less than three (3) minutes each.
rows.remedy: • Check thermostat wire connections (R, C, 1, & 2) • Check thermostat location in zone (too close to discharge grill)

rows.meaning: 05 – Open circuit (Compressor will not Run): • The ICC has had a protector trip for longer than 4 hours
rows.remedy: • Check for damaged, miswired, or wrong run capacitor • Check for broken wires, loose connectors, or miswired compressor • Check compressor windings for continuity • Check for open compressor internal protector

rows.meaning: 06 – Compressor Open Start Circuit: The ICC detects current in the Run circuit but not in the Start circuit of the compressor
rows.remedy: • Check for damaged, miswired, or wrong run capacitor • Check for broken wires, loose connectors, or miswired compressor • Check compressor windings for continuity

rows.meaning: 6L – Compressor Open Start Circuit: The ICC detects current in the Run circuit but not in the Start circuit of the compressor four (4) times in one compressor call
rows.remedy: • Check for damaged, miswired, or wrong run capacitor • Check for broken wires, loose connectors, or miswired compressor • Check compressor windings for continuity • Check for a compressor locked rotor

rows.meaning: 21 – Low Pressure Control Open: The ICC detects the LPC is open. Note: The low pressure control is ignored for the first 90 seconds of compressor operation
rows.remedy: • Unit has low refrigerant charge • Indoor coil is frozen (cooling mode) • Dirty indoor coil or filter (cooling mode) • Indoor blower is not running (cooling mode) • Outdoor coil is frozen (heating mode) • Expansion valve is not operating correctly

rows.meaning: 21L – Active Protection Low Pressure Control Trip
rows.remedy: LPC has opened 3 times in the same cooling operation, the ICC has locked out the compressor to protect it. ICC alternately flashes L and 21

rows.meaning: 29 – High Pressure Control Open: The ICC detects the HPC is open
rows.remedy: • Outdoor coil is dirty (cooling mode) • Outdoor fan is not running (cooling mode) • Dirty indoor coil or filter (heating mode) • Indoor blower is not running (heating mode) • Liquid line restriction • Excessive refrigerant charge

rows.meaning: 29L – Active Protection High Pressure Control Trip
rows.remedy: LPC has opened 3 times in the same cooling operation, the ICC has locked out the compressor to protect it. ICC alternately flashes L and 29

rows.meaning: No Voltage Compressor
rows.remedy: • Check to ensure power to compressor is correct • Check capacitor

rows.meaning: Welded Relay
rows.remedy: • Check system to ensure proper operation

rows.meaning: 83 – Condenser Coil Temperature Fault: The sensor detects an abnormally low or high coil temperature
rows.remedy: • Replace the sensor • Check sensor is installed correctly on control

rows.meaning: 84 – Outdoor Ambient Temperature Fault: The sensor detects an abnormally low or high outdoor ambient temperature
rows.remedy: • Check unit placement – If the outdoor unit is in a high temperature area, wait until the ambient temperature drops and check sensor reading. • Replace the sensor. • Check sensor is installed correctly on control

rows.meaning: 93 – Internal Control Fault: The control is not functioning properly.
rows.remedy: • Check control for proper system operation. • Replace control

rows.meaning: d1 – No Shared Data
rows.remedy: • Replace memory card with correct system information.
